source: "I love this city," Maria said.
correct: Maria said she loved that city.
Maria said that she loved that city.
hint: Backshift: love → loved. Shift: this → that
explanation: Estilo indirecto: retroceso verbal de presente → pasado, this → that.

source: "I will help you tomorrow," John said.
correct: John told me he would help me the next day.
John told me that he would help me the next day.
hint: will → would, you → me, tomorrow → the next day
explanation: Retroceso verbal: will → would. También se aplican cambios de pronombre y de tiempo.

source: "Are you coming to the party?" she asked.
correct: She asked if I was coming to the party.
She asked whether I was coming to the party.
She asked me if I was coming to the party.
hint: Yes/No question → if/whether + statement order
explanation: Las preguntas de sí/no en estilo indirecto usan if/whether + sujeto + verbo (orden de afirmación).

source: "Where did you buy that jacket?" he asked.
correct: He asked where I had bought that jacket.
He asked me where I had bought that jacket.
hint: Keep 'where' + statement order + backshift
explanation: Las preguntas con wh- conservan la palabra interrogativa pero cambian a orden de afirmación con retroceso verbal.

source: "Close the window," the teacher said to us.
correct: The teacher told us to close the window.
hint: Commands → told + object + to-infinitive
explanation: Órdenes en estilo indirecto: told + persona + to + verbo base.

source: "Don't be late!" my mother said.
correct: My mother told me not to be late.
hint: Negative commands → told + object + not to
explanation: Órdenes negativas en estilo indirecto: told + persona + not + to + verbo base.

source: "Could you open the door, please?" she said.
correct: She asked me to open the door.
She asked us to open the door.
hint: Requests → asked + object + to-infinitive
explanation: Peticiones en estilo indirecto: asked + persona + to + verbo base.

source: "I have never been to London," he said.
correct: He said he had never been to London.
He said that he had never been to London.
hint: have been → had been (present perfect → past perfect)
explanation: Retroceso verbal: presente perfecto → pasado perfecto.

prompt: Report this statement with time/place shifts
source: "I'm working here today," she said.
correct: She said she was working there that day.
She said that she was working there that day.
hint: here → there, today → that day, am → was
explanation: Retroceso verbal + cambio de lugar (here → there) + cambio de tiempo (today → that day).

source: "I can't come to the meeting," he said to me.
correct: He told me he couldn't come to the meeting.
He told me that he couldn't come to the meeting.
hint: can't → couldn't
explanation: Retroceso verbal: can → could (forma negativa: can't → couldn't).

source: "What are you doing now?" she asked me.
correct: She asked me what I was doing then.
She asked me what I was doing at that moment.
hint: now → then/at that moment, are → was
explanation: Cambio de tiempo: now → then. Retroceso verbal: are → was. Orden de afirmación.

source: "Let's go to the cinema," Tom said.
correct: Tom suggested going to the cinema.
Tom suggested that we go to the cinema.
Tom suggested we should go to the cinema.
hint: Let's → suggested + -ing or that + subject + go
explanation: Sugerencias en estilo indirecto: suggested + gerundio o suggested that + sujeto + verbo base.

source: "I was sleeping when you called," she said.
correct: She said she had been sleeping when I called.
She said that she had been sleeping when I called.
hint: was sleeping → had been sleeping (past continuous → past perfect continuous)
explanation: Retroceso verbal: pasado continuo → pasado perfecto continuo.

prompt: Report this yes/no question using 'wanted to know'
source: "Have you finished the report?" my boss asked.
correct: My boss wanted to know if I had finished the report.
My boss wanted to know whether I had finished the report.
hint: if/whether + had finished (present perfect → past perfect)
explanation: Variación del verbo introductorio: wanted to know = asked. Se aplica el retroceso verbal.

source: "I forgot to send the email," he said.
correct: He admitted that he had forgotten to send the email.
He admitted he had forgotten to send the email.
He admitted forgetting to send the email.
hint: Different reporting verb. forgot → had forgotten
explanation: Estilo indirecto con 'admitted': admitted + cláusula con that o + gerundio.

source: "I don't understand this exercise," she said.
correct: She said she didn't understand that exercise.
She said that she didn't understand that exercise.
hint: don't → didn't, this → that
explanation: Retroceso verbal: presente negativo → pasado negativo. this → that.

source: "I missed the bus because I woke up late," he said.
correct: He explained that he had missed the bus because he had woken up late.
He explained he had missed the bus because he had woken up late.
hint: Different reporting verb. missed → had missed, woke up → had woken up
explanation: Retroceso verbal doble: pasado simple → pasado perfecto en ambas cláusulas.

source: "I will call you tonight," he said.
correct: He promised he would call me that night.
He promised that he would call me that night.
hint: will → would, tonight → that night
explanation: Estilo indirecto con 'promised': will → would, tonight → that night.

source: "Why is she crying?" he said.
correct: He wondered why she was crying.
hint: Keep 'why' + statement order + backshift
explanation: 'Wondered' introduce preguntas indirectas sin necesidad de 'asked'. Se mantiene el orden de afirmación.

source: "Don't touch that wire!" the electrician said.
correct: The electrician warned me not to touch that wire.
The electrician warned us not to touch that wire.
hint: Warnings → warned + object + not to
explanation: Advertencias en estilo indirecto: warned + persona + not + to + verbo base.
